Scouting Summary

Common themes

  • Right Medium, averaging 128.2 kph (up to 136.8).
  • Typical length is 6-7m (their good length); median 7.0 m.
  • Stock ball is a good length outside off, swinging away, seaming both ways, passing outside off (33% of deliveries).
  • Round the wicket to LHB 58% · over the wicket to RHB (round 1%).
  • Round the wicket he shifts his pitching line from 6th stump to stumps.
  • Across an over he hammers a repeatable length.

Biggest threats

  • Most dangerous length is Full (8 wkts, 2.3% adjusted strike).
  • Danger pitching line: Down leg.
  • Takes 30% of wickets pitching a good length on the 6th stump, mostly over the wicket (78%).
  • Beats the bat 10.7% of tracked balls (false-shot 19.5%).
  • Gets you bowled more than most — 24% of his wickets (1.3× the typical rate for this type).
  • 74% of catches are behind the wicket (keeper / slips / gully); most often to keeper, slip: 1st, slip: 2nd.

Areas to exploit

  • Concedes most runs pitching a good length wide outside off (17% of runs).
  • Short ball: 20% of deliveries, economy 3.4 — 2 wkts from 404 short balls.
  • Away from full, the wicket threat drops off — look to score in the less-productive lengths.
  • Most of his runs leak square/through the off side (50%) — his main scoring release.

Solid line = career, dotted = last 3 years (where enough recent balls). Percentile within same-type peers (grey = the peer distribution, line = this bowler). Release/crease vs hand × pace/spin; movement/speed/repeatability vs pace/spin. Release & speed are modern-era (2017+ / partial). Crease variation = how much he moves his release point sideways across the crease from ball to ball (within his main angle): a high percentile = he varies where he lets the ball go a lot, a low percentile = he releases from the same spot every ball. Repeatability = length consistency over his stock-length band (2–11 m, so deliberate yorkers and bouncers don't count as poor control): a high percentile = tighter, more metronomic lengths than peers; a low percentile = he varies his length more. A marker at the very edge = he sits beyond the typical peer range on that trait.

Sequencing & Over Construction

Metronomic — hammers the same length repeatedly, little to feast on (length spread ±1.4 m; more repeatable than 91% of pace bowlers); holds a steady length right through the over; and holds the same crease position through the over.
Across 28 dismissals, his wicket ball is close in length and pace to the delivery before it — he builds pressure with repetition, not a big change-up.
